clinician.final_diagnosis: Histopathology revealed a completely excised low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 33-year-old man presented with lower abdominal pain and fullness, and a palpable right lower quadrant mass following abdominal trauma. An abdominal ultrasound identified a well-circumscribed lesion in the right mid-lower abdomen, which was noted as distinct from the small bowel and appendix. Surgical intervention involved a right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis. Intraoperatively, a large inflammatory abdominal lesion with associated enlarged lymph nodes was visualized within the mesentery of the ascending colon, and the appendix was not visualized. The known final diagnosis, based on subsequent histopathology, was a completely excised low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with lower abdominal pain, fullness, and a palpable mass after abdominal trauma.

Abdominal ultrasound revealed a well-circumscribed lesion in the right mid-lower abdomen, distinct from the small bowel and appendix, with debris, increased echogenicity, and no intrinsic vascularity.

Intraoperatively, a large inflammatory abdominal lesion with associated enlarged lymph nodes was visualized within the mesentery of the ascending colon; the appendix was not visualized. A right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis was performed.
The known final diagnosis is a completely excised low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes.
